newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish Aksa to raise 1997 turnover to $460 mln.
newsitem.headline: Turkish Aksa to raise 1997 turnover to $460 mln.

text.p: Turkey's leading acrylic fibre, tow and tops producer Aksa Akrilik Kimya Sanayii A.S. targets a $460 million turnover in 1997, compared with the $400 million expected in 1996, a senior company official said.

"We increased our turnover to $400 million in 1996, from $310 million in 1995 and the market conditions will help us to realise a $460 million turnover in 1997," Selcuk Ergin, the general manager of the company, told Reuters.
Company shares listed on the Istanbul Stock Exchange ended at 19,500 lira on Friday, up from Thursday's 19,250 lira.
Aksa increased its annual production capacity by 10,000 tonnes to 200,000 tonnes in the begining of 1996, the biggest capacity in a single plant on the world.
Ergin said the company decided to increase the capacity to 230,000 in 1997, in light of encouraging market conditions.
A $40 million investment will be completed in two stages -- a 15,000-tonne capacity increase in June and another 15,000-tonne rise in September.
The company has an additional 80,000-tonne capacity expansion investment for which it applied to secure government incentives, like tax reductions in December 1996.
"We hope to get the incentive certificate soon and to begin the project in late 1997," Ergin said.
The new investment will take 2-1/2 years to complete.
"We began production with 3,500 tonnes 27 years ago as the smallest company in the world and in 2-1/2 years we will become the largest acrylic fibre and tow producer in the world," Ergin said.
"We will have 310,000 tonnes of output capacity in three years and pass Molte Fibre which currently has 310,000 tonnes of capacity because they decided to close one of their three plants," he added.
He said Aksa's annual turnover would reach $600 million when all investments are finished.
The company increased its total exports to $200 million in 1996 from $166 million in 1995.
Aksa also plans to produce acrylonitril, the raw material for its production and polypropilen, the raw material for plastic materials.
"But we postponded our plans due to the uncertainities on Petkim's privatisation," Ergin said.
Petkim, Turkey's only petrochemicals producer, has been a privatisation candidate since 1987.
Ergin said his company would like to join any consortium buying into the Petkim float.
"Or we can make a long-term contract to invest in the acrylonitril production unit of the company with the consortium which will buy the company," he said.
Meanwhile, Aksa is negotiationg with two global producers to make a joint investment to produce polypropilen.
"We are negotiating with the biggest and the third biggest producers in the world," he added.

Aksa reported 18.7 trillion lira of turnover in the first nine months of 1996, up from 12.9 trillion lira in the same 1995 period while its net profits leapt to 3.9 trillion lira from 1.8 trillion lira in January-September 1995.
